25um Gene-Expression Atlas: Region-Decoding Baseline

genomics
gene-expression
AGEA
decoding
anatomy
First-pass region-decoding accuracy on the preliminary, un-denoised 25um EBRAINS gene-expression volumes, ahead of a PPCA-based denoise/impute pipeline.
Author

Olivier Winter

Published

August 31, 2026

Overview

The existing AGEA denoise/impute pipeline (06-denoise-impute.py) merges hemispheres, fills missing genes per voxel via PPCA across genes, and corrects a slice-to-slice staining artefact (“curtaining”) on the 200um Allen Gene Expression Atlas (AGEA). We are extending this to 25um, using a new, much higher-resolution gene-expression dataset — Carey, Piluso, Bjerke et al. (2026), An interactive 3D atlas of gene expression in the mouse brain, bioRxiv — which re-registers over 401,000 ISH sections (4,083 genes) to the Allen CCF at 25um.

Before the raw, mask-carrying dataset is available, we ran a first pass on a preliminary, already-interpolated (not yet denoised/imputed) export of the same 4,083 genes, to (a) validate the tooling end-to-end on the real data format and (b) establish a reference region-decoding accuracy.

Method

  • Format: one NIfTI (.nii.gz) per gene, (566, 320, 456) voxels, 25um isotropic, uint8-quantized. No separate anatomical registration or data-availability mask ships with this preliminary export.
  • Atlas registration: this NIfTI grid is not natively bregma-registered like iblatlas.atlas.AllenAtlas. Its axis order matches Allen’s (ap, dv, ml) by voxel count (dv=320, ml=456 match exactly; ap=566 vs. Allen’s 528, i.e. 38 voxels of extra padding). The AP offset was found empirically by maximizing the Dice overlap between this dataset’s cross-gene “ever nonzero” brain footprint and AllenAtlas(res_um=25).label != 0: nifti_ap = allen_ap + 14 (no shift needed on dv/ml), Dice = 0.995.
  • Resolution & sampling: rather than an arbitrary voxel subsample at 25um, each gene volume was cropped to the aligned window and mean-pooled 8x8x8 down to 200um — the resolution 06-denoise-impute.py trains at — reusing the region-label volume the same way, mode-pooled (following the aggregation convention already used in 05-generate-atlas-templates.py). All 62,879 in-brain voxels were used — no subsampling, mirroring the original pipeline’s use of the full brain.
  • Decoding: StandardScaler + PCA (50 components) on the pooled (62879, 4083) matrix, then an MLPClassifier (hidden_layer_sizes=(50,)) predicting Allen and Cosmos region labels, evaluated under two train/test splits: a plain random 80/20 split (matches the original script) and a spatially-grouped split (600um blocks held out whole, to check for leakage from spatial autocorrelation between adjacent voxels).

Results

Region level Split Accuracy
Cosmos (11 classes) random 0.936
Cosmos (11 classes) spatial block 0.920
Allen (fine-grained) random 0.746
Allen (fine-grained) spatial block 0.679

The random-vs-block gap at both levels is consistent with spatial-autocorrelation leakage in the random split — larger at Allen level, where regions are smaller and more sensitive to nearby-voxel leakage. The top 50 PCA components explain ~46% of gene-expression variance, leaving room to improve once the data is properly denoised/imputed.

Conclusion

Even on preliminary, un-denoised 25um data, region identity is well recovered from gene expression alone (92% Cosmos, 68% Allen, spatially-held-out). This is a solid reference point: format handling, atlas registration, and the decoding harness all work end-to-end on the real EBRAINS-derived data, ahead of building the PPCA-based denoise/impute pipeline for the final raw, mask-carrying dataset.

## Overview

The existing AGEA denoise/impute pipeline
([`06-denoise-impute.py`](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/iblatlas/blob/main/iblatlas/genomics/gene_expression_scrapping/06-denoise-impute.py))
merges hemispheres, fills missing genes per voxel via PPCA across genes, and corrects a
slice-to-slice staining artefact ("curtaining") on the 200um Allen Gene Expression Atlas
(AGEA). We are extending this to 25um, using a new, much higher-resolution gene-expression
dataset — Carey, Piluso, Bjerke et al. (2026),
[*An interactive 3D atlas of gene expression in the mouse brain*](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.01.20.700446),
bioRxiv — which re-registers over 401,000 ISH sections (4,083 genes) to the Allen CCF at 25um.

Before the raw, mask-carrying dataset is available, we ran a first pass on a preliminary,
already-interpolated (not yet denoised/imputed) export of the same 4,083 genes, to
(a) validate the tooling end-to-end on the real data format and (b) establish a reference
region-decoding accuracy.

## Method

- **Format**: one NIfTI (`.nii.gz`) per gene, `(566, 320, 456)` voxels, 25um isotropic,
  uint8-quantized. No separate anatomical registration or data-availability mask ships with
  this preliminary export.
- **Atlas registration**: this NIfTI grid is not natively bregma-registered like
  [`iblatlas.atlas.AllenAtlas`](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/iblenv/_autosummary/iblatlas.html#module-iblatlas).
  Its axis order matches Allen's `(ap, dv, ml)` by voxel count (`dv=320`, `ml=456` match
  exactly; `ap=566` vs. Allen's `528`, i.e. 38 voxels of extra padding). The AP offset was
  found empirically by maximizing the Dice overlap between this dataset's cross-gene
  "ever nonzero" brain footprint and `AllenAtlas(res_um=25).label != 0`:
  `nifti_ap = allen_ap + 14` (no shift needed on `dv`/`ml`), **Dice = 0.995**.
- **Resolution & sampling**: rather than an arbitrary voxel subsample at 25um, each gene
  volume was cropped to the aligned window and mean-pooled 8x8x8 down to 200um — the
  resolution `06-denoise-impute.py` trains at — reusing the region-label volume the same
  way, mode-pooled (following the aggregation convention already used in
  [`05-generate-atlas-templates.py`](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/iblatlas/blob/main/iblatlas/genomics/gene_expression_scrapping/05-generate-atlas-templates.py)).
  **All 62,879 in-brain voxels** were used — no subsampling, mirroring the original
  pipeline's use of the full brain.
- **Decoding**: `StandardScaler` + `PCA` (50 components) on the pooled `(62879, 4083)`
  matrix, then an `MLPClassifier` (`hidden_layer_sizes=(50,)`) predicting Allen and Cosmos
  region labels, evaluated under two train/test splits: a plain random 80/20 split (matches
  the original script) and a spatially-grouped split (600um blocks held out whole, to check
  for leakage from spatial autocorrelation between adjacent voxels).

## Results

| Region level | Split | Accuracy |
|---|---|---:|
| Cosmos (11 classes) | random | 0.936 |
| Cosmos (11 classes) | spatial block | 0.920 |
| Allen (fine-grained) | random | 0.746 |
| Allen (fine-grained) | spatial block | 0.679 |

The random-vs-block gap at both levels is consistent with spatial-autocorrelation leakage
in the random split — larger at Allen level, where regions are smaller and more sensitive
to nearby-voxel leakage. The top 50 PCA components explain ~46% of gene-expression
variance, leaving room to improve once the data is properly denoised/imputed.

## Conclusion

Even on preliminary, un-denoised 25um data, region identity is well recovered from gene
expression alone (92% Cosmos, 68% Allen, spatially-held-out). This is a solid reference
point: format handling, atlas registration, and the decoding harness all work end-to-end
on the real EBRAINS-derived data, ahead of building the PPCA-based denoise/impute pipeline
for the final raw, mask-carrying dataset.
